Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; this is untested theorycraft resting on 3.2.0 PTR values that may be revised. It is deliberately a contrarian build. Every source says Barbarian bleed was nerfed in 3.2.0, and they are right about the headline: Two-Handed Sword Expertise's bleeding bonus was halved from 30%[x] to 15%[x] and the Hemorrhage node went 75%[x] to 60%[x]. But Ring of the Ravenous was not simply nerfed, it was reworked - its duration and damage came down (6-8s to 4-6s, 60-80% to 40-60%) while it gained the ability to apply a Rend stack and had its cooldown halved from 1 second to 0.5. A shorter, weaker, twice-as-frequent effect that also applies stacks is a different item, not a worse one. The hypothesis is that Rend-stack application rate now matters more than per-stack magnitude, which would make a fast-hitting Rend build better than the raw numbers suggest. Honest framing: no source supports this, the consensus reading is that Barbarian bleed is dead, and this build exists to test whether the consensus read the rework as a nerf without checking the cooldown line.

Rotation
  1. Keep War Cry and Challenging Shout up, sustain Fury with Lunging Strike, and apply Rend continuously rather than in bursts.
  2. The rhythm is faster and shallower than old Rend play, because application frequency is the whole point.
Variants

Leveling — Shouts up, Lunging Strike for Fury, Rend on packs. Nothing distinctive yet - the build does not exist until Ring of the Ravenous is on.
Move on when Level 70, Torment 1, and Ring of the Ravenous in hand. Run the stack-counting test in test_notes the moment you equip it, before investing further.

Early Endgame — Shouts up, Lunging Strike to sustain Fury, Rend continuously rather than in bursts - the whole point is application frequency. Ring of the Ravenous is now on a 0.5 second cooldown instead of 1 second, so the correct rhythm is faster and shallower than Season 14 Rend play. Count stacks; this stage is data collection.
Move on when The stack-count test has passed - roughly double application rate confirmed, and Rend damage confirmed to scale per stack rather than merely refresh. If either check fails, stop and play barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor instead. That is not a fallback, it is the correct answer to a failed hypothesis.

Late Endgame — Rend on repeat with shouts maintained, Lunging Strike whenever Fury dips. Test the Scorching upgrade's new fire wave here: no source anywhere describes it, so whether it scales with Rend stacks or is flat is genuinely unknown and worth ten minutes on a dummy.
Move on when This build only graduates to pushing if it has beaten barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor in a direct comparison at equal gear. If it merely competes, report that as the finding and push the meta build instead.

Pushing — Untested at push tiers and unlikely to reach them - be blunt about that. The most probable outcome is that this hypothesis fails at test step two, because damage-over-time stacks that only refresh a duration are common in this game and the patch notes give no reason to think Rend is different. It is written out in full anyway because a rework with a halved cooldown deserves ten minutes of testing before an archetype is written off on a headline nerf, and a PTR is exactly where that ten minutes costs nothing. All values are 3.2.0 PTR values and may change before Season 15 launches.

PTR status: no filter targets a post-3.2.0 Rend Barbarian because the consensus is that the archetype is dead - this build is an untested contrarian hypothesis. Reuses the diablo4lootfilter.com Finder verified reachable 2026-08-08 (diablofilter.com/browse: HTTP 403 twice, unreachable). Search class Barbarian for a same-class code and preview it before applying; expect to unhide bleed and Rend-relevant affixes that a Whirlwind or Upheaval code will have filtered out.

Uniques
  • ring PTR route: PTR Boosts from the vendor Mrak next to the main Waypoint in any major city. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0; it exists in Season 14's general unique pool, so expect a lair-boss target farm or the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe. The entire hypothesis is this item - do not attempt the build without it. Where →
  • helm PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route (Season 14, unchanged): general unique pool - lair-boss target farm or the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe on a Common helm. Where →
  • pants PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route (Season 14, unchanged): Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe on Common pants (1 Enhanced Primordial Dust and 10 Primordial Dust) rather than a dedicated boss. Where →
  • amulet PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0. Its PTR change - double damage now includes Healthy enemies - suits a bleed build unusually well, since Rend stacks are applied at the start of a fight when everything is still healthy. Where →
  • SSplinter of Hellfire jewelry socket New Soul Splinter socketable, jewelry only. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts include Soul Splinters. Live route: unpublished. This is the rare build that should genuinely consider Hellfire over Anguish: it deals 40-100% increased damage at the cost of 100% Critical Strike Chance, and if this build's damage really is dominated by Rend damage-over-time stacks rather than by critical hits, the trade is favourable. That 'if' is untested and is part of what the build is for. Verify on a dummy - compare Hellfire against Anguish directly - before committing, and expect Anguish to win if Rend turns out to crit. Where →
  • Target-farm Duriel, King of Maggots, a Greater-tier Lair boss (1x Greater Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →
  • offhand Mythic Unique with no dedicated boss: every Lair boss can drop it, or craft it in the Horadric Cube with Pandemonium Fragments - remembering that only one Cube-crafted Mythic may be equipped at a time. Where →

Point allocation, in order62 points across 10 nodes

[ptr] Provenance, stated plainly. No 3.2.0 skill tree is published for any build on any site - the official notes carry no allocations, and Maxroll, Icy Veins, d4builds and d4guides were all still serving Season 14 guides on 2026-08-08, day 5 of the 8-day PTR. This allocation is therefore the specialist's, built from the skill list the PTR digest authorises for this class plus the 3.2.0 changes that actually apply. Treat the point counts as a starting shape to test, not as a published build. Where a skill's upgrade mods are named below, those names are carried over from Season 14 planner data - 3.2.0 does not rename them. Where a skill appears with no mods, that is deliberate: its mod names were not published anywhere consulted, and inventing them would be worse than leaving them out. On the PTR you can skip this stage outright - Mrak's boosts grant level 70 and maxed aspects directly - so this allocation is written for what a live Season 15 would look like.

Skill point priority

  1. Rend to max - the build is an application-rate experiment and Rend is what gets applied
  2. Lunging Strike for Fury generation, still capped at 0.5 Fury per 1% Maximum Life since 3.1.x
  3. War Cry for Berserking and Vulnerable
  4. Challenging Shout for damage reduction - a melee bleed build on a class that lost 27% of its baseline scaling needs it
  5. Leap for gap closing
  6. Wrath of the Berserker as the ultimate for its flat +30% all damage

Skill point priority

  3. War Cry and Challenging Shout maxed
  4. Rallying Cry for Fortify and Unstoppable only; its Madawc variant was halved 200% to 100% on the PTR, so do not rank it for damage
  5. Wrath of the Berserker as the ultimate

Board & glyph focus

Attack Speed and Bleeding routes first - if the hypothesis is right, application rate is the scaling stat and attack speed buys application rate. Then survivability. Explicitly do not route through Hemorrhage or Blood Rage expecting Season 14 value: both were cut on the PTR (75%[x] to 60%[x] and 60%[x] to 45%[x]), and this build's case does not depend on them.

Board & glyph focus

Attack Speed, Bleeding and survivability routes maxed. Two hard avoids carried from the meta build. Ramaladni's Magnum Opus: on the PTR it drains 10% of Maximum Fury rather than a flat 10 per second, which punishes any build that wants a full bar to sustain a generator loop. Skills to select2 picks

  • ValiancePerk

    Raheir's perk: a rotating cheat-death that negates any hit worth 15% or more of your current Life.

  • InspirationPassive

    The damage multiplier that makes Raheir an offensive hire and not only a defensive one.

How to run them

[ptr] 3.2.0 changes nothing about mercenaries - the words "Mercenary" and "Mercenaries" and all four mercenary names are absent from the official 3.2.0 notes entirely. So this is the Season 14 pairing carried over, which is the only guidance that exists. Hire Raheir for Valiance's rotating cheat-death and Inspiration's damage multiplier, and reinforce with Varyana on Bloodthirst for attack speed. One PTR-specific point worth making: Barbarian's core stat scalar was cut 1.1 to 0.8, so the class is measurably squishier per point of Strength than it was in Season 14 - if you find yourself dying on the PTR where you did not before, swapping Varyana for Aldkin's Field of Languish is the honest response, and it is a pairing Maxroll already endorses for Barbarian.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; this is untested theorycraft resting on 3.2.0 PTR values that may be revised. It is deliberately a contrarian build. Every source says Barbarian bleed was nerfed in 3.2.0, and they are right about the headline: Two-Handed Sword Expertise's bleeding bonus was halved from 30%[x] to 15%[x] and the Hemorrhage node went 75%[x] to 60%[x]. But Ring of the Ravenous was not simply nerfed, it was reworked - its duration and damage came down (6-8s to 4-6s, 60-80% to 40-60%) while it gained the ability to apply a Rend stack and had its cooldown halved from 1 second to 0.5. A shorter, weaker, twice-as-frequent effect that also applies stacks is a different item, not a worse one. The hypothesis is that Rend-stack application rate now matters more than per-stack magnitude, which would make a fast-hitting Rend build better than the raw numbers suggest. Honest framing: no source supports this, the consensus reading is that Barbarian bleed is dead, and this build exists to test whether the consensus read the rework as a nerf without checking the cooldown line.

Rotation
  1. Keep War Cry and Challenging Shout up, sustain Fury with Lunging Strike, and apply Rend continuously rather than in bursts.
  2. The rhythm is faster and shallower than old Rend play, because application frequency is the whole point.
Variants

Leveling — Shouts up, Lunging Strike for Fury, Rend on packs. Nothing distinctive yet - the build does not exist until Ring of the Ravenous is on.
Move on when Level 70, Torment 1, and Ring of the Ravenous in hand. Run the stack-counting test in test_notes the moment you equip it, before investing further.

Early Endgame — Shouts up, Lunging Strike to sustain Fury, Rend continuously rather than in bursts - the whole point is application frequency. Ring of the Ravenous is now on a 0.5 second cooldown instead of 1 second, so the correct rhythm is faster and shallower than Season 14 Rend play. Count stacks; this stage is data collection.
Move on when The stack-count test has passed - roughly double application rate confirmed, and Rend damage confirmed to scale per stack rather than merely refresh. If either check fails, stop and play barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor instead. That is not a fallback, it is the correct answer to a failed hypothesis.

Late Endgame — Rend on repeat with shouts maintained, Lunging Strike whenever Fury dips. Test the Scorching upgrade's new fire wave here: no source anywhere describes it, so whether it scales with Rend stacks or is flat is genuinely unknown and worth ten minutes on a dummy.
Move on when This build only graduates to pushing if it has beaten barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor in a direct comparison at equal gear. If it merely competes, report that as the finding and push the meta build instead.

Pushing — Untested at push tiers and unlikely to reach them - be blunt about that. The most probable outcome is that this hypothesis fails at test step two, because damage-over-time stacks that only refresh a duration are common in this game and the patch notes give no reason to think Rend is different. It is written out in full anyway because a rework with a halved cooldown deserves ten minutes of testing before an archetype is written off on a headline nerf, and a PTR is exactly where that ten minutes costs nothing. All values are 3.2.0 PTR values and may change before Season 15 launches.

Uniques
  • ring PTR route: PTR Boosts from the vendor Mrak next to the main Waypoint in any major city. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0; it exists in Season 14's general unique pool, so expect a lair-boss target farm or the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe. The entire hypothesis is this item - do not attempt the build without it. Where →
  • helm PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route (Season 14, unchanged): general unique pool - lair-boss target farm or the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe on a Common helm. Where →
  • pants PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route (Season 14, unchanged): Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe on Common pants (1 Enhanced Primordial Dust and 10 Primordial Dust) rather than a dedicated boss. Where →
  • amulet PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0. Its PTR change - double damage now includes Healthy enemies - suits a bleed build unusually well, since Rend stacks are applied at the start of a fight when everything is still healthy. Where →
  • SSplinter of Hellfire jewelry socket New Soul Splinter socketable, jewelry only. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts include Soul Splinters. Live route: unpublished. This is the rare build that should genuinely consider Hellfire over Anguish: it deals 40-100% increased damage at the cost of 100% Critical Strike Chance, and if this build's damage really is dominated by Rend damage-over-time stacks rather than by critical hits, the trade is favourable. That 'if' is untested and is part of what the build is for. Verify on a dummy - compare Hellfire against Anguish directly - before committing, and expect Anguish to win if Rend turns out to crit. Where →
  • Target-farm Duriel, King of Maggots, a Greater-tier Lair boss (1x Greater Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →
  • offhand Mythic Unique with no dedicated boss: every Lair boss can drop it, or craft it in the Horadric Cube with Pandemonium Fragments - remembering that only one Cube-crafted Mythic may be equipped at a time. Where →

Reasoning

HypothesisRing of the Ravenous' halved cooldown (1s to 0.5s) plus its new Rend-stack application means total Rend uptime and stack count roughly double, which more than compensates for the 25-33% cut to its own duration and damage. If Rend damage scales with stack count, a build built for application rate beats one built for per-hit magnitude even after the Two-Handed Sword Expertise bleeding cut from 30%[x] to 15%[x].
Confidencelow
How to test itConfidence is low deliberately - this contradicts every source read. Test cheaply and be willing to abandon it. (1) On a dummy, count Rend stacks applied per ten seconds with Ring of the Ravenous equipped versus not. If the halved cooldown does not translate into roughly double the application rate, the premise is wrong at step one. (2) Confirm whether Rend damage actually scales per stack or whether stacks only refresh a duration. This is the load-bearing unknown and the patch notes do not answer it - if stacks merely refresh, the whole build collapses and should be abandoned without further testing. (3) Compare total damage against barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor at equal gear. The meta build's Ring of Red Furor occupies the same ring slot conceptually, so this is a genuine either-or, not a complement. (4) Check whether the Scorching upgrade's new fire wave scales with Rend stacks or is a flat effect - the aggregators do not mention it at all, so this may be entirely unexplored ground or entirely worthless. (5) Watch survivability: a bleed build fights at melee range with a class that just lost 27% of its baseline scaling.

Provoke

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 25 seconds

Raheir Taunts enemies around you for 5 seconds. You gain 5% Damage Reduction for each target, up to 20%.

Ground Slam

Core skillRaheir

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Round Shield

Basic Attack: Shield Strike

Raheir brutalizes the ground, dealing 160% Physical damage and Slowing enemies by 30% for 6 seconds. Targets in the center of the slam are Slowed by 60% instead.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Raheir swings a round shield at enemies, dealing 85% Physical damage. Every 20 swings, Raheir Heals you for 8% of your Maximum Life.

Shield Charge

Core skillRaheir

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Tower Shield

Basic Attack: Shield Bash

Raheir rushes forward aggressively, dealing 110% Physical damage and Taunting nearby enemies for 4 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Raheir bashes enemies with a tower shield, dealing 80% Physical damage and Fortifying you for 0.2% of your Maximum Life.

Crater

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Raheir strikes the ground 3 times, each burst dealing 30% Physical damage and Pulling In enemies. The final burst deals 40% more Physical damage and additionally Stuns enemies for 2 seconds.

Raheir's Guard

PassiveRaheir

Raheir grants you 15%[+] Armor.

Vanguard

PassiveRaheir

Raheir Slows surrounding enemies by 40%.

Mocking Lure

PassiveRaheir

You deal 15%[x] increased damage to enemies Taunted by Raheir.

Iron Wolf's Ward

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he Knocks Back Close enemies and Taunts Distant enemies for 4 seconds.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Iron Wolf's Call

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, your next 4 Core Skills within 10 seconds deal 25%[x] increased damage and cost no Resource.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 25%.

Sundering Shield

PassiveRaheir

Raheir's final Crater burst deals 200%[x] increased damage and inflicts Vulnerable on enemies for 4 seconds.

Shield Throw

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Raheir throws his shield, dealing 450% Physical damage and Taunting enemies for 5 seconds. The shield bounces up to 9 times and cannot bounce to the same target twice.

Iron Wolf's Arrival

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he also casts Ground Slam and Shield Throw.

Raheir's Valiance's Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Consecrated Shield

PassiveRaheir

Raheir's Shield Throw Consecrates enemies for 6 seconds. Directly damaging a Consecrated enemy Heals you for 6% of your Maximum Life, once per target.

Bastion

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 30 seconds

Raheir takes a protective position for 5 seconds, redirecting 90% of the damage that would be dealt to surrounding allies to himself for 5 seconds.

Bastion's initial cast also grants surrounding allies Unstoppable for 1.0 seconds.

Iron Wolf's Virtue

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he Heals you for 25% of your Maximum Life.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Inspiration

PassiveRaheir

Enemies affected by Raheir's Ground Slam take 15%[x] increased damage.

Allies affected by Raheir's Bastion deal 25%[x] increased damage.

Raheir's Aegis

PassiveRaheir

Raheir grants you 15% Resistance to All Elements.

Draw Fire

PassiveRaheir

When you use a Healing Potion, Raheir Taunts enemies around him for 4 seconds. Can only occur once every 20 seconds.
